To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DIP and its related methods can be interpreted as the manifold modeling in embedded-space (MMES) which is based on a novel tensor modeling method.
the convolution operation can be divided into two parts: delay-embedding and transformation, and that delay-embedding can be regarded as a kind of low-dimensional manifold modeling.

the proposed MMES can be used for interpreting the DIP, and the convolution operation can be interpreted by a combination of the delay-embedding and the transformation (encoder-decoder) for image/tensor modeling in embedded space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two main contributions: 1) proposing an interpretable and explainable image/tensor modeling approach for image restoration and enhancement, 2) providing a new perspective to understand the DIP.

the following two points: (1) proposing an interpretable and simple image/tensor modeling approach, (2) characterizing the DIP and convolution operation for image processing from a perspective of dynamical systems and manifold modeling.
